LevelNameStrings.name: Overworld level name text and builder
summary: Word-based level name text: names are three words picked by [$00]/[$01]. Characters: A-Z = $00-$19, $1F = space, $5D = apostrophe, $5A = # (digits probably $64+);
bit 7 marks the last character of a word. Three pointer tables (DATA_049C91, DATA_049CCF, DATA_049CED) give each word's offset; $01CB is the blank word.
$049D07: writes a stripe image record for the name into the buffer at $7F:837B (VRAM $508B, 19 tiles, attribute $39), blank-padded and $FF-terminated.
Parameters: [$00]-[$01]: name code. [$01] & $7F = word 1, [$00] high nibble = word 2, [$00] low nibble = word 3.
$049D9A, $049DD1, $049E22, $049E4C: overworld processes for switching between Mario and Luigi (fade out, swap player state, fade in).
$049E52: star warp lift-off (player flies up the screen). $049E9B: unused divide-by-10 loop.

s049EA7.name: Table: path tile movement offsets
summary: Two bytes per overworld tile (tile number - 1), loaded into [$00]/[$01] by the path movement code at $049725. Exact meaning (per-tile step distances) inferred.

s049F49.name: Table: path tile flags
summary: Two bytes (0 or 1) per overworld tile (tile number - 1), loaded into [$04]/[$05] by the path movement code at $049720. Probably marks which axis is used.

s049FEB.name: Table: overworld tile properties
summary: One byte per overworld tile (tile number - 1), read into [$0E] at $0495EF. Value $14 sets [$1B80] = 1. Meaning of the other values (0, 4, 8, $C) not verified.

s04A03C.name: Table: corner path tile numbers
summary: 24 tile numbers, mostly path corners ($4D is the bridge exit). Searched when leaving a level tile. Entry index selects rows of the tables at $04A054, $04A084 and $04A0E4.

s04A054.name: Table: corner tile step bytes
summary: Byte pairs per entry of the corner tile table at $04A03C, read at $0496FF. Exact meaning not verified.

s04A084.name: Table: corner tile X/Y offsets
summary: 24 entries of two signed 16-bit values (X offset, Y offset), 4 bytes each, indexed by entry * 4 in the corner tile table at $04A03C (read at $0493A4). Label $04A086 starts at the second word of entry 0.

s04A0E4.name: Table: corner tile direction flags
summary: One byte per corner tile entry. Bit 1 set means the first offset is used as the Y offset instead of X; the sum with [$0DD6] picks the player.
